primitives.name: Noise-Tolerant Encoding
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Encoding features:** (1) empty values in a pattern match any value; (2) *missin
primitives.assumptions: Missing and gap events are modeled as stochastic perturbations within a bounded tolerance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Exceeds tolerance thresholds for missing/gap counts leads to pattern misalignment.

layer2.mapping: Maps noisy event sequences to symbolic pattern templates; supports robustness against observation errors.
layer2.telemetry: Number of missing values, gap frequency, pattern overlap ratio

primitives.name: LSH Acceleration
primitives.verbatim_quote: Per-pattern caps: empty values ≤ |p|; missing values ≤ ||p||/10 (at most 1 per event); gaps ≤ |p|-1.
primitives.assumptions: Co-occurrence sparsity allows efficient candidate filtering via hash-based similarity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High cardinality or dense co-occurrence graphs degrade LSH efficacy.

layer2.mapping: Enables scalable pattern generation by reducing candidate space via locality-sensitive hashing.
layer2.telemetry: Candidate pruning rate, LSH collision frequency, runtime improvement

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that multivariate pattern mining must balance compression efficiency (MDL) with interpretability (effectiveness). The method uses a minimum description length formulation to optimize pattern sets such that the total description length of the data under those patterns is minimized. This dual objective ensures that discovered patterns are both compact and informative. Noise-tolerant encoding allows for flexibility in matching sequences with missing or out-of-order events, which is essential for real-world applications like sports analytics. The use of LSH accelerates the search process by filtering unlikely pattern combinations early, improving scalability. The failure mode arises when the noise tolerance is exceeded or when LSH fails to capture relevant pattern interactions due to hash collisions or insufficient granularity.
